Global Articulation and Progression Scholarship T's & C's 145.21 KB NCUK The NCUK Articulation and Progression Scholarship supports international students progressing/articulating from an NCUK pathway programme to continue their studies at Aston University, Birmingham. The scholarship provides a tuition fee reduction for eligible students progressing/articulating from an NCUK International Foundation Year (IFY), International Year One (IY1), or Master's Preparation programme (MP) and enrolling at Aston University for the September 2026 intake. The scholarship is competitive and application-based , meaning applicants must submit a scholarship application to be considered. Meeting the eligibility criteria does not guarantee that a scholarship will be awarded. All applications are assessed in line with the published eligibility requirements and scholarship availability. Scholarships are applied as a tuition fee reduction to the eligible programme of study and cannot be exchanged for cash or transferred to another programme, applicant, or intake. Scholarship values The available scholarship awards for NCUK students progressing/articulating to Aston University are shown below. NCUK Students currently studying Scholarship Value NCUK International Foundation Year (IFY) £6,500 tuition fee reduction (first year at Aston University) NCUK International Year One (IY1) £5,000 tuition fee reduction in Year 2 (first year at Aston University), with the potential to receive an additional £5,000 in the final year of study NCUK Master's Preparation Programme (MP) £5,000 tuition fee reduction (first year at Aston University) For students progressing/articulating from NCUK International Year One , the scholarship may be awarded across two academic years . Students who meet the continuation requirements during their first year at Aston University may receive a further £5,000 tuition fee reduction in their final year of study. Continuation of the final-year award requires students to achieve an overall 60% average at first attempt , pass all modules at first attempt, and remain enrolled as an Overseas fee payer. How to apply To be considered for the NCUK Articulation and Progression Scholarship, applicants must complete the scholarship application form after receiving an offer to study at Aston University. Applicants will be asked to submit a short written statement as part of the application explaining why they should be considered for the scholarship. Applications are reviewed following the submission deadline. Where the number of eligible applications exceeds the available scholarship allocation, applications will be assessed competitively using the University’s internal evaluation process. Key dates Submission deadline: 14th June 2026 (midnight UK time) Scholarship outcome: 30th June 2026 Deposit deadline: 21st July 2026 (midnight UK time) Eligibility To be eligible for the NCUK Articulation and Progression Scholarship, applicants must: Be classified as an Overseas fee payer Hold an offer for a full-time Undergraduate or Postgraduate Taught programme at Aston University, Birmingham Be progressing/articulating directly from one of the following NCUK pathway programmes: NCUK International Foundation Year (IFY) NCUK International Year One (IY1) NCUK Master's Preparation programme (MP) Meet all academic and English language entry requirements Submit a completed scholarship application before the published deadline Pay the required programme deposit and enrol for the September 2026 intake. The scholarship is open to self-funded international students . Applicants whose studies are fully or partially funded by a sponsor are not normally eligible unless a formal agreement with Aston University confirms eligibility. Programme exclusions The following programmes are not eligible for the NCUK Articulation and Progression Scholarship. Undergraduate MBChB Medicine MPharm Pharmacy MOptom Optometry BSc Nursing Studies BSc Healthcare Science (Audiology) Postgraduate PGDip / MSc Overseas Pharmacy Assessment Programme (OSPAP) MSc Physician Associate Practice All MBA programmes All MRes programmes All research-only programmes. Additional programme exclusions may apply where specified by the University. Here are some simple steps to help you stay on top of the pennies. Paying Your Deposit All International students and Home postgraduate students will be required to pay a deposit to secure a place on their chosen course. The exceptions are: Undergraduate and postgraduate students who take out a student loan Government-sponsored students Your deposit will then be deducted from your first-year tuition fees. Details of how and when to pay your deposit will be outlined in your offer letter. If you have any questions, please contact the Admissions team. Funding Your Studies How you can fund your studies: Student loan Receiving bursaries and scholarships from Aston Parental contributions Working part-time Loans There are two types of student loan to help you cover the costs of university. You pay these loans back after you finish your course, when you’re earning over £25,000 per year. Tuition fee loan: available to undergraduate students from the UK, tuition fee loans are paid directly to your university or college by the Government. You can expect to be paid any amount up to the maximum, which equals the cost of fees per year. Maintenance loan: available to full-time undergraduate students from the UK, maintenance loans help pay for living costs such as food, travel, rent, course materials and accommodation. The amount you are awarded is dependent on household income. The maximum loan you can receive is £10,277 per year. For more information regarding applying for Student Finance England as a Home student, please visit: Home Students | Aston University Support It's important to us that your time at University is as enjoyable, productive and worry-free as possible, so there are plenty of places at Aston for advice on money matters. Our friendly and experienced Student Advisor's in the Aston University Student Advice Team offer information on a number of different funds, trusts and bursaries you can apply to for financial support. In the Students' Union's Student Advice Centre offers extensive independent information, advice and representation services. Both of  these team's expertise covers a wide range of areas, including tuition fees and financial worries. Our hardship fund is called  the Aston Student Support Fund It’s reassuring to know that if finances get tricky during your studies, Aston University offers hardship funds that can help you get back on track. Find out more here . Scholarships for 2026/27 entry We offer a range of scholarships to ensure that anyone who is qualified to come to Aston University can do so, regardless of their financial circumstances. We are committed to supporting the most talented and hardworking students to achieve their potential through schemes that help lower tuition and living costs. Students do not need to apply to be considered for a scholarship because Aston University will use UCAS data, household income information provided by the Student Loans Company and information held on University records for placement years, to determine awards. Scholarship entitlement will normally be determined by the 30th November 2026. Students who are eligible for one or more of the Aston Scholarships will receive communications concerning their award/s through My Aston Portal (MAP). Are you an international student? We also offer a range of scholarships designed exclusively to support you. Scholarships for UK students are listed below: Aston Support Scholarship Successful applicants will be awarded £1,250 every year of their degree, totalling £5,000. Available to UK students classed as care leavers, young carers and estranged students, children from a military family or refugees. No application necessary. The University will automatically assess your eligibility using information on your A Level (or other) results provided by UCAS or at enrolment. The number of Aston Support Scholarships is not limited. If you have been selected to receive this scholarship, we will contact you. Aston Forward Scholarships Forward Scholarships are funded by alumni and friends of Aston. As of 2026/7, they are worth a total of £5000 across your degree (or £8000 for Medical students), with £2000 awarded to all recipients in the first year and £1500 in the second and final years (and in each year of study for Medical students). Available to UK students with a household income of less than £25,000, these scholarships will not be awarded on financial need or academic achievements alone. The scholarships will be awarded to students with amazing ambitions; students wanting to create a better world through community activity or business ideas, or to those who have overcome significant barriers to study at Aston. It is necessary to apply for Forward Scholarships. You will be invited to apply once you have completed the pre-enrolment process on My Aston Portal. Application dates for 2026 are 19th August to 5th October. Any applications received after this date will not be considered. A limited number of Aston Forward Scholarships are available. Aston University must receive your household income assessment, carried out by the Student Loans Company (SLC) . We strongly advise you to start this process now. You do not need to take a loan to prove your household income, information as how to do this can be found here View full details on the Aston Forward Scholarships page. Aston Placement Scholarship Successful applicants will be awarded £1,250 to support living expenses during their placement year. In order to receive the Placement scholarship, you must have an Approved placement record on MAP at the time of payment, which will be the end of November 2026. Details on how to get your placement approved, and the Placement guidance pages can be found here Placement Year: Essential Information | Aston University Available to UK students with a household income of £42,875 or below, those taking an unpaid placement year, or those undertaking a placement abroad. No application necessary. If you are selected to receive the scholarship, the university will let you know at the start of your placement year or once your placement details have been finalised - you will need to have registered your placement activity for Term 1 by 1st November 2026. For students where the assessment is based on household income, the university will normally make an assessment in year one. Aston Aspirational Scholarship Available to UK students with a household income of up to and including £42,875. Successful applicants will be awarded £500 in year one of their study. No application necessary. The University will automatically assess your eligibility using information provided at enrolment. The number of Aston Aspiration scholarships is not limited. If you have been selected to receive this scholarship, we will contact you shortly after your place at Aston has been confirmed. The Ernest Edward Scholarships for Asylum Seekers Aston University is delighted to offer up to four sanctuary scholarships for students who are seeking refuge in the UK. These scholarships will benefit asylum seekers or those who have been granted a form of limited permission to stay in the UK, following an unsuccessful asylum application, and who are therefore prevented from accessing student finance. Find out more and apply. MSc Motorsport Scholarship Programme Aston University is excited to introduce the MSc Motorsport Scholarship Programme, designed exclusively for home students. This initiative presents an exciting chance for aspiring minds to pursue a master's degree in MSc Future Vehicle Technologies. Through this pioneering opportunity, we aim to support and uplift talented individuals from underrepresented backgrounds, promoting diversity and excellence within the dynamic automotive industry. Undergraduate Home students receive all scholarship payments through the Aston Journey Portal (excluding tuition fee discounts). Once funds have been released, you will receive an email to your Aston email address confirming that your scholarship funds are available to be withdrawn. How do I access the Aston Journey Portal? You can log on to the Aston Journey Portal via www.astonjourney.co.uk . I don't have log-in details for the Aston Journey Portal? If you have not previously received a payment via the Aston Journey Portal, your account has not yet been created. Your account will be created when your first payment is released, and you will receive an email to your Aston email address with your account log-in details. You are encouraged to change the original password that you will receive to one you that you are more likely to remember. How do I change my Aston Journey password? Once you have an Aston Journey account, you can reset your password here . Once the funds have been released to my Aston Journey account, how do I withdraw the funds? Log on to Aston Journey and watch a short video of the withdrawal process here . When do I need to withdraw my funds by? You have until 31st July to withdraw any available funds. After this date, funds will be removed from your Aston Journey account. Once removed, funds cannot be reinstated. I am struggling to access the Aston Journey Portal/withdraw my funds, who can I contact? If you are having trouble accessing your funds, please contact Aston Journey directly. Their email address is: Student.Info@AstonJourney.co.uk. If you have a query about the scholarship itself or the award, please contact ug_scholarships@aston.ac.uk. This may be an employer, government body or embassy (not a family member). You need to inform the University as soon as possible once your sponsorship is confirmed by sending us an approved official Financial Guarantee Letter (FGL). Depending on the conditions of your sponsorship, you may still be required to pay the tuition fee deposit or the tuition fees. The University will send a tuition fee invoice as instructed in the Financial Guarantee Letter. This page should explain how the process works and answer any questions you have. How it Works Step by Step Applicant submits a program application to Aston University Applicant receives and accepts the program offer from Aston University Applicant/Sponsor shares the Financial Guarantee Letter (FGL) with Aston University (Admissions team and sponsor team) The deposit payment requirement will be waived, if the sponsor is paying the tuition fees to the University. In all other cases, the student is still responsible for the deposit payment. Applicant follows the normal CAS and VISA application process, and enrols *Applicant needs to make sure the sponsor settles the tuition fee payment* Your Financial Guarantee Letter (FGL) Please include the following information in your Financial Guarantee Letter (FGL): Student name, Aston ID University and program name Date of the letter, the period or dates the sponsorship covers Full details of where the invoice should be addressed including an email address Contact details of the sponsor Bank details of the sponsor The amount of money the sponsor is contributing for tuition fees and living costs OR a statement that the official sponsor will cover all of your fees and maintenance S haring of personal information between the University and your sponsor You will sign a consent form regarding the sharing of your information with your sponsor during your study at the university. This can include information related to your offer, academic results, engagement etc. The Sponsored Student's Responsibilities Submit your FGL to sponsors@aston.ac.uk and admissions team. Ensure the fees are settled by your sponsor or yourself. You are liable for any outstanding payments during your study, any related debts could affect your progression and graduation at the university. Fulfil any requirements from your sponsors, such as obtaining and providing related documents, maintaining the required attendance rate, academic results etc. Update the university if there are any changes to your sponsorship status or any other details. Submit an updated FGL if the period of study is extended, this could be due to repeating years, leave of absence etc. Other Frequently Asked Questions What happens if I only secure my sponsorship at a later stage of the admissions process? Please submit the Financial Guarantee Letter (FGL) to the University as soon as possible once you have confirmed the sponsorship to sponsors@aston.ac.uk . The team will then update the relevant records. What happens if I have paid the deposit myself already? You can submit a refund request in the My Aston Portal (MAP) system for the deposit payment you have made. Your sponsor would receive an invoice with the full tuition fee. Am I eligible for any university scholarships? No, sponsored students are not eligible for any university scholarships. Scholarships are for fully self-funded students only. What happens if my sponsor does not pay the fee accordingly? You will be liable for all the outstanding payments personally. Unable to clear the outstanding payment could affect your access to resources, progression and graduation at the university etc. This would also affect your credit score. UG ICS TERMS SEPTEMBER 2027 › 01 / 10 Purpose and scope
This document outlines the eligibility and conditions for full-time, self-funded international
undergraduate applicants to receive the Undergraduate International Community Scholarship
(UG ICS) at Aston University for the September 2027 intake.
Eligibility is assessed in line with the published criteria and these Terms and Conditions.
The Scholarship is applied by the University using its internal systems and is subject to
successful enrolment.
These Terms and Conditions are correct at the time of publication and may be subject
to change.
AUTOMATIC AWARD: NO APPLICATION NEEDED
The UG ICS is an automatic scholarship. There is no application process. Applicants who
meet the published eligibility criteria and satisfy all conditions will receive the Scholarship,
triggered by payment of the programme deposit and subject to successful enrolment.
UG ICS TERMS SEPTEMBER 2027 › 02 / 10 1 GENERAL PROVISIONS › › ›
1.1  To be eligible for the Undergraduate International Community Scholarship (UG ICS),
applicants must be classified as Overseas for tuition fee purposes.
1.2  Applicants must hold an offer for a full-time, taught undergraduate degree programme
delivered on campus at Aston University, Birmingham, commencing in September 2027.
1.3  Applicants must be entering the first year of study of their undergraduate
degree programme.
1.3a  Applicants must be applying to Aston University directly. Applicants progressing or
articulating under any formal partnership, progression, or articulation agreement are not
eligible for this Scholarship and should refer to the dedicated partnership scholarship
applicable to their route, as set out in clause 2.3.
1.4  Applicants must meet all academic and non-academic conditions stated in their offer letter.
1.5  Applicants must be self-funded. Students whose tuition fees are wholly or partially funded
by a sponsor are not eligible, unless the sponsor has an official written agreement with Aston
University confirming eligibility for scholarship consideration.
1.6  The UG ICS is an automatic scholarship. There is no application process, and no
scholarship application form is required.
1.7  Meeting the eligibility criteria does not create an unconditional entitlement to the
Scholarship. The Scholarship is awarded only once all eligibility, offer conditions, deposit
payment, and enrolment requirements have been satisfied.
1.8  In order for the scholarship to be applied, applicants must:
pay the required programme deposit by the deadline stated in their offer letter; and
successfully enrol by the latest enrolment date for their September 2027 programme.
1.9  These Terms and Conditions constitute the authoritative and governing terms of the
Undergraduate International Community Scholarship. In the event of any inconsistency
between these Terms and Conditions and information provided by a member of University
staff, representative, agent, or third party, whether verbally or in writing, these Terms and
Conditions shall prevail. The University shall not be bound by any representation, advice, or
information that is inconsistent with these published Terms and Conditions.
UG ICS TERMS SEPTEMBER 2027 › 03 / 10 2 SCHOLARSHIP BASIS AND EXCLUSIONS › › ›
2.1  Automatic, non-competitive award
The Undergraduate International Community Scholarship (UG ICS) is an automatic, non-
competitive award for eligible undergraduate applicants. There is no application process.
Eligibility is assessed against the published criteria and these Terms and Conditions. The
Scholarship is triggered by payment of the programme deposit and becomes active on
successful enrolment.
2.2  Programme exclusions
The following programmes are not eligible for the Undergraduate International
Community Scholarship:
BSc Nursing Studies (Adult Nursing or Mental Health)
MBChB Medicine
MOptom Optometry
MPharm Pharmacy
BSc Healthcare Science (Audiology)
2.3  Partnership, progression, and articulation exclusions
Applicants progressing or articulating to Aston University under any formal partnership,
progression, or articulation agreement are not eligible for the Undergraduate International
Community Scholarship. Dedicated partnership scholarships are available to these
applicants instead.
This exclusion applies regardless of whether the applicant applies for, is offered, accepts,
declines, or is found ineligible for the partnership scholarship applicable to their route, and
regardless of the value of that award. Declining or failing to secure a partnership scholarship
does not create eligibility for the Undergraduate International Community Scholarship.
For the avoidance of doubt, this exclusion includes (but is not limited to) applicants progressing
via a foundation, pathway, international year one, or preparatory programme delivered by a
partner institution or pathway provider, and applicants articulating from a partner university, in
each case under a formally approved agreement with Aston University.
UG ICS TERMS SEPTEMBER 2027 › 04 / 10 2 SCHOLARSHIP BASIS AND EXCLUSIONS · CONTINUED › › ›
Where an applicant is identified as progressing under a partnership, progression, or articulation
agreement at any stage, including after an Undergraduate International Community Scholarship
has been offered or applied to the student record, the University reserves the right to withdraw
that award and to apply the correct partnership scholarship in its place. The application of an
award in error does not create an entitlement.
2.4  Applicants who remain eligible
Applicants applying to Aston University directly, and who are not progressing under any formal
partnership, progression, or articulation agreement, remain eligible, subject to meeting all other
eligibility requirements set out in these Terms and Conditions.
Applicants who have completed, or are required to complete, an Aston University pre-sessional
or preparatory course (including, but not limited to, pre-sessional English language or study
skills programmes) remain eligible, provided they are entering directly into the first year of an
eligible undergraduate degree programme and are not progressing under a partnership,
progression, or articulation agreement.
Aston University’s determination of whether an applicant is progressing under a partnership,
progression, or articulation agreement is final.
APPLICANTS FROM A PARTNER INSTITUTION
If you’re joining Aston through one of our partner institutions or pathway providers, you have
your own dedicated partnership scholarship. Speak to your partner institution or our
International Office to confirm which award applies to your route.
UG ICS TERMS SEPTEMBER 2027 › 05 / 10 3 SCHOLARSHIP TRIGGER, ACTIVATION, AND AVAILABILITY › › ›
3.1  There is no application process for the Undergraduate International Community
Scholarship. Eligible applicants are identified by the University from their applicant record, and
no scholarship application form, statement, or supporting submission is required.
3.2  Payment of the required programme deposit by the deadline stated in the offer letter is the
trigger for consideration of the Scholarship.
3.2a  The deadline for the Scholarship is the offer deadline for the applicant’s Aston University
application, as stated on their offer letter. Applicants who do not meet the requirements of their
offer, including payment of the programme deposit, by that deadline will not receive the
Scholarship. The University does not publish a separate scholarship deadline, and offer
deadlines may differ between applicants.
3.3  The Scholarship becomes active only upon successful enrolment, which requires the
applicant to have:
met all conditions of their offer;
paid the required programme deposit;
successfully enrolled within the required enrolment period and latest arrival date; and
received a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) and be holding a valid Student visa
or another visa type that permits study.
3.4  The Scholarship will be applied to the student record by the University using its internal
systems. Where a Scholarship has been applied in error, including due to administrative or
system error, Aston University reserves the right to amend or withdraw the award. The
application of a Scholarship in error does not create an entitlement.
3.5  The availability of the Undergraduate International Community Scholarship during Clearing
or any late application period is not guaranteed. The University reserves the right, at its sole
discretion, to allocate, withhold, vary, or withdraw scholarship availability during Clearing,
subject to demand and institutional priorities at the time. Where the Scholarship is made
available during Clearing, this will be communicated by the University and will remain automatic
based on deposit payment and subsequent enrolment.
3.6  The University reserves the right to amend, suspend, or withdraw the Scholarship where
required for operational, regulatory, or strategic reasons. Any discretion exercised in individual
cases does not create a precedent or entitlement for other applicants.
3.7  Applicants acknowledge that they should not make financial, immigration, or personal
decisions in reliance on the expectation of receiving the Scholarship until it has been formally
applied following successful enrolment.
UG ICS TERMS SEPTEMBER 2027 › 06 / 10 4 AWARDING THE SCHOLARSHIP › › ›
4.1  The scholarship is awarded as a tuition fee discount applied to the eligible undergraduate
programme of study. No cash alternative or cost-of-living payment is available.
4.1a  The total value of the Undergraduate International Community Scholarship is £9,000,
applied as a tuition fee discount across the eligible undergraduate programme of study,
distributed as follows:
Year 1: £3,000
Year 2: £3,000
Final year: £3,000
The scholarship applies to taught years only. Placement years, repeated years, and repeated
modules are excluded. Year 2 and the final year are awarded automatically on progression,
subject to the conditions set out in section 5.
4.1a(i)  The Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) will show the Scholarship as £3,000,
being the Year 1 payment only. The Year 2 and final year payments are conditional on
successful progression and are not guaranteed at the point the CAS is issued, so they are not
shown on the CAS.
4.1b  Applicants entering a Top-up BSc (Hons) programme (that is, direct entry into the final
year of a Bachelor’s degree) will receive the Year 1 payment of £3,000 only. As a Top-up
programme comprises a single year of study, the Year 2 and final-year payments do not apply.
4.2  A student may normally hold only one Aston University scholarship per programme of
study. Where a student is eligible for more than one scholarship or tuition fee discount, the
award of the highest value will usually apply.
4.2a  Notwithstanding clause 4.2, the University reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to
permit the Undergraduate International Community Scholarship to be held in combination with
a separate, specifically designated scholarship or tuition fee award, where this is expressly
approved and communicated by the University.
4.3  The scholarship is not transferable to another applicant, programme, intake, academic
year, or institution.
4.4  Scholarships are valid only for the September 2027 intake and cannot be deferred or
carried forward to a future intake.
UG ICS TERMS SEPTEMBER 2027 › 07 / 10 5 RECEIVING AND RETAINING THE SCHOLARSHIP › › ›
5.1  The scholarship will be applied to the student’s tuition fee account only after:
the programme deposit has been paid; and
the student has successfully enrolled within the required enrolment period.
5.2  The scholarship is applied to each taught year of study in line with the payment schedule
set out in clause 4.1a. Year 2 and the final year are applied automatically on progression,
subject to the conditions in this section.
5.3  Students must remain fully enrolled and in attendance, as defined by Aston University, to
retain the scholarship.
5.4  Students who withdraw from Aston University part-way through an academic year will no
longer be eligible for the scholarship. Any tuition fee discount already applied may be
withdrawn, and the student will be liable for the full tuition fee for that academic year.
5.5  Students repeating modules, whether with or without attendance, are not eligible to receive
the scholarship in respect of the repeated study.
5.6  Where a student suspends their studies and takes a Leave of Absence:
if the Leave of Absence covers a complete academic year, no tuition fee is charged, and no
scholarship is payable;
if the Leave of Absence is taken part-way through an academic year, scholarship eligibility
will be assessed in line with Aston University’s Tuition Fees Charging Policy and may be
adjusted on a pro-rata basis.
UG ICS TERMS SEPTEMBER 2027 › 08 / 10 6 APPEALS AND FINAL DECISION › › ›
6.1  Decisions relating to eligibility and award of the Scholarship are made in accordance
with these Terms and Conditions and internal University processes. The University’s decision
is final.
6.2  Appeals may only be made on the grounds of procedural error, defined strictly as a
demonstrable failure by the University to follow these published Terms and Conditions.
6.3  Appeals will not be considered based on:
academic judgement;
disagreement with eligibility outcomes;
failure to pay the programme deposit by the stated deadline;
failure to enrol by the latest enrolment date;
changes in personal or financial circumstances;
comparisons with other applicants or awards made; or
the availability or non-availability of the Scholarship during Clearing.
6.4  The University is not required to provide individual feedback on eligibility decisions, nor to
disclose internal assessments, operational checks, or deliberative materials.
6.5  Where no procedural error is identified, the original decision will stand and will not
be reconsidered.
6.6  Appeals must be submitted in writing to the Director of Student and Academic Services
within the timeframe specified by the University. Late or incomplete appeals will not
be accepted.
6.7  Evidence submitted after the final eligibility decision will not normally be considered unless
the applicant can demonstrate that the information could not reasonably have been made
available at the time.
6.8  The University will not enter into further correspondence regarding a scholarship decision
once the appeals process has concluded.

excludes research-only or research-led programmes, including MRes programmes.

The tuition fee deposit required to secure an offer of study, as specified in the applicant’s offer

The final date by which a student must enrol and commence attendance on their programme,

Enrolment
Completion of all registration, immigration, and attendance requirements as determined by
Aston University, including confirmation of eligibility to study in the UK.
Overseas

accordance with the University’s fee status assessment and applicable UK legislation and
regulations.
Self-funded
A student’s tuition fees are paid entirely by the student and are not wholly or partially funded,
reimbursed, or sponsored by any third party, employer, government, organisation, or external

SIR ADRIAN CADBURY CHANCELLOR'S SCHOLARSHIP › 01 / 10 Purpose and scope
These Terms and Conditions set out the eligibility criteria, application process, assessment
framework, award conditions, and appeals process for the Sir Adrian Cadbury Chancellor’s
Scholarship for international students commencing study at Aston University in the January
2027, April 2027, or September 2027 intake.
The scholarship honours the legacy of Sir Adrian Cadbury and supports students who
demonstrate integrity, social responsibility, and a commitment to making a positive impact
through their academic and professional ambitions.
The Sir Adrian Cadbury Chancellor’s Scholarship is a competitive, application-based award.
Meeting the eligibility criteria and submitting an application does not create any expectation,
entitlement, or presumption that a scholarship will be awarded.
Website content is provided for guidance only. In the event of any discrepancy between
website content and these Terms and Conditions, these Terms and Conditions shall
take precedence.
These Terms and Conditions are correct at the time of publication and may be amended
where necessary.
1 SCHOLARSHIP VALUE › › ›
1.1  The Sir Adrian Cadbury Chancellor’s Scholarship provides a £10,000 tuition fee reduction.
1.2  The scholarship is applied as a tuition fee waiver only and has no cash value.
1.3  The award cannot be used for deposits, accommodation, maintenance, or any other costs.
SIR ADRIAN CADBURY CHANCELLOR'S SCHOLARSHIP › 02 / 10 2 ELIGIBLE PROGRAMMES › › ›
2.1  The scholarship is available to applicants holding an offer for an eligible full-time
undergraduate or postgraduate taught programme delivered on campus at Aston University,
commencing in the January 2027, April 2027, or September 2027 intake, unless explicitly
excluded below.
2.2  The following postgraduate programmes are excluded from eligibility:
All MRes programmes SEPTEMBER ONLY
All MBA programmes ALL INTAKES
All PhD and research programmes ALL INTAKES
Overseas Pharmacists Assessment Programme (OSPAP) PgDip SEPTEMBER ONLY
MSc Physician Associate Practice SEPTEMBER ONLY
MPH Public Health SEPTEMBER ONLY
2.3  The following undergraduate programmes are excluded from eligibility:
BSc Nursing Studies (Adult Nursing) SEPTEMBER ONLY
BSc Nursing Studies (Mental Health) SEPTEMBER ONLY
MBChB Medicine SEPTEMBER ONLY
MOptom Optometry SEPTEMBER ONLY
MPharm Pharmacy SEPTEMBER ONLY
BSc Healthcare Science (Audiology) SEPTEMBER ONLY
2.3a  The exclusions in clauses 2.2 and 2.3 apply to the January 2027, April 2027 and
September 2027 intakes alike. Each excluded programme is tagged to show the intakes in
which it is delivered: those marked September only are not offered in January or April, while
those marked All intakes remain excluded whenever they are delivered. PhD and research
programmes have variable start dates that do not align with taught intakes, and are excluded
throughout. The tags are provided for guidance only and do not extend or limit the exclusions
set out above. Where an excluded programme is subsequently made available in any 2027
intake, whether or not it is currently delivered in that intake, applicants for that programme will
remain ineligible for the Scholarship.
2.4  Aston University reserves the right to amend the list of eligible or excluded programmes
where required for regulatory, professional, or strategic reasons.
SIR ADRIAN CADBURY CHANCELLOR'S SCHOLARSHIP › 03 / 10 3 ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA › › ›
Applicants must meet all of the following criteria at the point of application:
3.1  Be classified as an international (overseas fee-paying) student for tuition fee purposes.
3.2  Hold an offer for an eligible programme at Aston University for January 2027, April 2027, or
September 2027 entry.
3.3  Meet all academic, English language, and non-academic conditions stated in their offer
letter by the required deadlines.
3.4  Be self-funded. Applicants whose tuition fees are fully or partially funded by an external
sponsor are not eligible.
3.5  Successfully submit a completed scholarship application using the official personal
application link issued by Aston University.
3.6  Eligibility is assessed based on the applicant’s programme, funding status, and fee
classification as recorded at the scholarship application deadline. Subsequent changes to
programme choice, funding arrangements, or fee status will not be applied retrospectively.
SIR ADRIAN CADBURY CHANCELLOR'S SCHOLARSHIP › 04 / 10 4 APPLICATION PROCESS AND DEADLINES › › ›
4.1  The Sir Adrian Cadbury Chancellor’s Scholarship is a competitive, application-based award.
4.2  Eligible applicants will be issued a personal scholarship application link to the email
address recorded on their Aston University applicant record after receiving an offer to study.
4.3  It is the applicant’s responsibility to:
ensure their contact details are accurate;
check junk or spam folders; and
access and submit the application using the issued link.
Failure to receive or access the application link does not constitute grounds for appeal unless a
system error is formally confirmed by Aston University.
4.4  Applications submitted via any other route will not be considered.
4.5  Applicants must submit:
a completed application form; and
a written statement of approximately 500 words outlining how they intend to make a
positive impact and use their degree to support communities.
Statements of 550 words or more, or of 450 words or fewer, will be excluded
from assessment.
SIR ADRIAN CADBURY CHANCELLOR'S SCHOLARSHIP › 05 / 10 4 APPLICATION PROCESS AND DEADLINES · CONTINUED › › ›
4.6  An application is deemed submitted only once an automated submission confirmation has
been issued. Incomplete, draft, or unconfirmed applications will not be assessed.
4.7  Application deadlines, decision timelines, and application windows will be published on
Aston University’s website: aston.ac.uk/international/scholarships.
4.8  It is the applicant’s responsibility to consult the published webpage and ensure submission
by the stated deadline. The University is not responsible for missed deadlines resulting from
failure to consult published information.
4.9  Where the number of eligible applications exceeds the number of available awards,
scholarships will be allocated following a competitive assessment process. The University is
not required to award a scholarship to all eligible applicants.
SIR ADRIAN CADBURY CHANCELLOR'S SCHOLARSHIP › 06 / 10 5 AWARD BASIS, EXCLUSIVITY, AND SUPERSESSION › › ›
5.1  Due to the high value of the award, the Sir Adrian Cadbury Chancellor’s Scholarship
cannot be held in conjunction with any other internally or externally managed scholarship,
bursary, fee discount, or tuition fee award, unless explicitly confirmed otherwise in writing by
Aston University.
5.2  Where an applicant is eligible for, or has been offered, more than one scholarship or tuition
fee discount, only one award may be held per programme of study.
The single award of the highest monetary value will normally apply, as determined by
Aston University.
Where the Sir Adrian Cadbury Chancellor’s Scholarship represents the highest value award, it
will supersede all other scholarships or fee discounts.
The University’s determination of the applicable award is final.
5.3  Applicants progressing from foundation providers, pre-masters providers, or via formal
progression or articulation agreements remain eligible to be considered, subject to meeting all
other eligibility requirements.
5.4  Where a progression-, pathway-, or partner-specific scholarship or tuition fee discount
exists, the award of the Sir Adrian Cadbury Chancellor’s Scholarship, if greater in value, will
override and replace any such alternative award if the applicant is successful.
SIR ADRIAN CADBURY CHANCELLOR'S SCHOLARSHIP › 07 / 10 6 RECEIVING AND RETAINING THE SCHOLARSHIP › › ›
6.1  The scholarship will be applied to the student’s tuition fee account only after:
the required programme deposit has been paid;
the appropriate SITS scholarship code has been applied to the student record; and
the student has successfully enrolled within the required enrolment period.
Where applicable, the scholarship is also conditional upon the student having received a
Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) and holding a valid Student visa.
6.2  Unless otherwise stated, the scholarship applies to tuition fees only and to the approved
academic year of entry. No cash alternative is available.
6.3  Students must remain fully enrolled and in attendance, as defined by Aston University, in
order to retain the scholarship.
6.4  Students who withdraw part-way through an academic year will no longer be eligible for the
scholarship. Any tuition fee reduction already applied may be withdrawn, and the student will be
liable for the full tuition fee for that academic year.
6.5  Students repeating modules, whether with or without attendance, are not eligible to receive
the scholarship in respect of the repeated study.
6.6  Where a student suspends their studies and takes a Leave of Absence:
if the Leave of Absence covers a complete academic year, no tuition fee is charged and no
scholarship is payable;
if taken part-way through an academic year, scholarship eligibility will be assessed in line
with Aston University’s Tuition Fees Charging Policy and may be adjusted on a pro-rata
basis.
6.7  Where sector-wide UKVI processing delays or external visa issues materially affect
enrolment, Aston University may, at its sole discretion, review eligibility on a case-by-case
basis. Such review does not guarantee continuation of the scholarship and does not establish
a precedent.
SIR ADRIAN CADBURY CHANCELLOR'S SCHOLARSHIP › 08 / 10 7 APPEALS AND FINAL DECISION › › ›
7.1  Scholarship decisions are made by a University selection panel operating in accordance
with internal procedures. No member of staff outside the designated process has authority to
vary or overturn a decision.
7.2  Appeals may be made only on the grounds of procedural error, defined as a demonstrable
failure by Aston University to follow the published application or assessment process, which
must be clearly evidenced and materially relevant to the outcome.
7.3  Appeals will not be considered on the grounds of:
academic judgement or comparative merit;
the content, quality, or score of an application;
disagreement with the outcome of the assessment;
the exercise of panel discretion;
the availability, allocation, or exhaustion of scholarship awards; or
comparisons with other applicants or awards made.
7.4  The University does not provide individual feedback on unsuccessful applications
and is not required to disclose scores, rankings, thresholds, assessor comments, or
panel deliberations.
7.5  Appeals must be submitted in writing within fourteen (14) calendar days of the tuition fee
invoice being raised on the applicant’s student record. The invoice date is used solely to
calculate the appeal submission window and does not constitute confirmation of scholarship
eligibility or award.
7.6  Where no procedural error is identified, the original decision will stand and will not be
reconsidered. Failure to submit an appeal within the stated timeframe will be taken as
acceptance of the original decision.
7.7  Once the appeals process has concluded, the University will not enter into
further correspondence.
SIR ADRIAN CADBURY CHANCELLOR'S SCHOLARSHIP › 09 / 10 8 WITHDRAWAL, AMENDMENTS, AND LIABILITY › › ›
8.1  Aston University reserves the right to withdraw the scholarship if information provided
by the applicant is found to be false or misleading, or if the student no longer meets the
eligibility criteria.
8.2  The University accepts no liability for costs incurred by applicants in connection with the
scholarship application process.
8.3  Aston University reserves the right to amend or withdraw the scholarship where required
for regulatory, operational, or strategic reasons.

The interview is an opportunity for us to get to know you, and for you to ask us anything about our MBA programme. During the interview we will also assess your suitability for a scholarship. How to get the best from your interview In this video Yasmin Ansari, Careers Consultant explains how to get the best from your interview. MBA Scholarships 2026/2027 We offer MBA scholarships to candidates who demonstrate the potential to make a transformational impact on the MBA cohort and a global impact through their subsequent career. All scholarships are awarded on the basis of a recommendation to an award panel after interview.  The criteria to be considered for a scholarship are: (Candidates must demonstrate at least two of these three criteria): 1.    Evidence of very strong academic performance (at least Upper Second Class Degree or equivalent) 2.    Evidence of considerable management experience of at least seven years 3.    Strong evidence of a mindset, attitude and skill set which will contribute to the MBA cohort. The MBA Scholarship offers will be as follows: Gold scholarships Gold Scholarships of £12,500 will to a small number of outstanding candidates. We are looking for: Evidence of leadership demonstrated throughout your career to date Evidence of entrepreneurial behaviours and impact Evidence of a commitment to equality, social responsibility and sustainability The ability to show the role that the Aston MBA will play in your career development. Silver scholarships Silver Scholarships for students of £6,500 will be awarded to candidates who are assessed as excellent. We are looking for: Evidence of commercial success achieved during your career to date Evidence of applying entrepreneurial thinking Understanding of the importance of equality, social responsibility and sustainability A passion for self-development, a clear rationale for wishing to study the Aston MBA and a vision of where the MBA will take you. In addition, we will be offering a few Aston 2030 scholarships . These are equivalent to Gold Scholarships (£12,500). Aston Inclusive The applicant has provided evidence via application and interview that they have increased the diversity and inclusion within an organisation over a period of normally at least seven years.  Further corroborating information may be sought. Aston Entrepreneurial The applicant has demonstrated via application and interview that they have set up, run and grown a business over a period of normally at least seven years.  Further corroborating information may be sought. Aston Transformational The applicant has demonstrated via application and interview that they have used their role within an organisation to transform that organisation in terms of growth, sustainability and intrapreneurship over a period of normally at least seven years.  Further corroborating information may be sought. MBA applicants would also be eligible to apply for the Vice-Chancellors Enterprise Award. No applicant may be awarded more than ONE scholarship. The process of awarding scholarships: Interviewers will recommend award A Scholarship panel will make the decision to offer scholarships We will include a deadline for MBA applicants to accept their offer and be eligible for their MBA scholarship offer. We will use the reply by date as the date for applicants to accept and take advantage of the scholarship. INTERNATIONAL SCHOLARSHIP SCHEME TERMS & CONDITIONS:  
 2025/26 ACADEMIC YEAR INTAKE 
1. Purpose and Scope  
1.1. This document outlines the eligibility and assessment criteria for full-time International 
fee paying students to receive scholarships from Aston University. This policy is correct 
at the time of publishing (October 2024) but may be subject to change.  
1.2. Applicants who are classed as Home for tuition fee purposes should consult 
http://www.aston.ac.uk/scholarships/ and navigate to the UK student scholarship pages 
of the Aston website for details of available scholarships and terms and conditions.  
1.3. This policy applies to applicants who are classed as Overseas for tuition fee purposes. 
The relevant scholarship awards and their application criteria can be found at  
https://www2.aston.ac.uk/scholarships/international. 
1.4. The International Scholarships Scheme is subject to the terms and conditions set out in 
this document. The University reserves the right to terminate a scholarship where a 
student is in breach of any of these terms and conditions, or, if any information 
provided to the University as part of a scholarship application is found to be false or 
misleading. In such circumstances, the student will be liable for any tuition fees 
incurred.  
1.5. Joint or externally funded scholarships may be subject to different terms and conditions. 
 
2. General Provisions  
2.1 A student may be eligible for an Aston International Scholarship if:  
2.1.1 They are classed as an Overseas student for tuition fee purposes;  
2.1.2 They are holding an offer for a full-time taught programme at Aston 
University, Birmingham campus, which will start in 2025/26  
academic year (autumn, winter and spring terms);  
2.1.3 They are entering into the first year of study on a degree 
programme taught by Aston University, Birmingham campus;  
2.1.4 They meet all of the conditions set out in their offer letter;  
2.1.5 They pay their programme deposit (if applicable) by the deadline 
stipulated in their offer letter;  
2.1.6 They complete any application requirements and meet any 
additional criteria required for the scholarship schemes being 
offered, as set out on our website for each individual scholarship 
scheme.  
2.2 A student who has all or part of their fees paid by a sponsor will not be eligible for 
an Aston Scholarship unless that sponsor has an official agreement confirming 
eligibility with Aston University.  
2.2.1 Sponsors include, but are not limited to, His Majesty’s UK 
Government, overseas governments or another national body, the 
British Council or any international organisation, any international 
company, or any other university.  
2.3 Any student considered to be in debt to Aston University will not be eligible to 
receive a scholarship award in full or in part.  
2.3.1 For the purposes of this policy, a student will be considered to be in 
debt to the University if they have received the third notice that a 
payment is overdue.   2.4 A student may only receive one Aston University discount/scholarship per 
programme studied, unless otherwise stated in writing as part of a specific 
scholarship/discount scheme.   
2.5 Where a student is eligible for more than one scholarship/discount the student will 
be awarded the one of the highest value.  
2.6 Successful scholarship applicants will be awarded a scholarship in the form of a 
discount on their tuition fees for the first year of study only, unless otherwise 
advertised. Applicants will be informed by the Scholarship Panel the level of 
scholarship which has been awarded to them.  
2.7 Scholarships advertised for multiple years of study will be reconfirmed at the start 
of each academic year; you must fulfil the requirements below: 
2.7.1 Maintenance of an average grade equivalent to an upper second-
class degree grade at Aston University and passing all modules of 
study at first attempt.  
2.7.2 Pass all modules without any re-assessments of any assessment 
components (retake of examination, coursework, test etc.) 
2.8 At Aston’s discretion, clauses 2.2-2.7 may be waived under specific conditions or for 
specific scholarships schemes or campaigns. Details of any waiver will be set out on 
our website.  
 
3. Applying for a Scholarship  
3.1 Applications for International Scholarships must be made by following the 
instructions set out on our website for each scholarship. Failure to follow these 
instructions fully may render an application void.  
3.2 There are a number of different categories of scholarships. Under some 
categories, student’s eligibility will be assessed automatically by the University’s 
Admissions Office based on the information provided in the application to study 
on an Aston University degree programme. Students who are eligible for 
scholarship categories which automatically apply, will receive an offer of a 
scholarship from Aston’s Admissions Office.  
3.3 The University reserves the right to limit the number of awards under certain 
scholarship schemes, this will be indicated on the web site when the scholarship 
is announced. The deadline for the application or consideration for the awards 
will also be stated on the web site. 
3.3.1 The University may change the number of awards and move the 
application deadline by providing a minimum of 30 days notice to 
the students on the website.  
3.3.2 Where there is a limited number of awards available, the 
consideration and award allocation may be conducted on a first 
come first served basis. In such cases the scholarship scheme will be 
closed without notice once all awards are accepted. 
3.4 Other categories of scholarship require an additional scholarship application to 
be submitted, usually in the form of a short personal statement or a video, or an 
interview to be conducted. Please consult our website for more information on 
how to apply for each scholarship scheme before submitting the application. 
Students are required to confirm that any material submitted as part of their 
application is their own work and does not infringe the intellectual property  rights of a third party. The Use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in scholarship 
application will render the application void. Scholarship interviews must be 
undertaken by the student who has applied for the scholarship.  
3.4.1 Any scholarship applications with materials not accessible to Aston 
University staff to review and assess will not be considered and not 
be eligible for later reconsideration.  
3.4.2 Aston University has the right to re-use scholarship application 
material in future marketing campaigns.  
3.5 In order to be awarded a scholarship, a student must meet the scholarship 
application deadline of the particular scholarship award. For automatic 
scholarships, this means accepting the course place before the acceptance 
deadline, outlined in the offer letter. For application or interview-based 
scholarships, this means completing the scholarship application form through 
our website by the deadline stated for that particular scholarship award which 
will be advertised on our website.  
3.6 Scholarship applicants should read in full the scholarship application and 
eligibility criteria prior to applying for a scholarship, as set out on our website.  
3.7 Students are entitled to apply for more than one scholarship award; however, 
students will only be awarded one scholarship, of the highest value (see 2.2-2.7).  
3.8 Applications will only be considered for international students holding an offer 
to study a full-time taught programme at Aston’s Birmingham campus in the UK.  
3.9 Students studying online, via blended learning, part time or any other method of 
learning, research programmes are not eligible for scholarships covered by these 
terms and conditions.  
3.10 Some scholarship awards come with additional benefits or responsibilities, 
for example, working as an ambassador for Aston University. Any additional 
benefits or responsibilities will be listed on Aston’s website.  
 
4. Approving and Awarding of Scholarships 
4.1 Scholarships are a discount made against the tuition fee applicable to the 
specific programme of study that the student is seeking to enrol upon. No cash 
or cost of living alternative is available.  
4.2 Scholarship entitlement will normally be approved before the commencement of 
the degree programme. It is not possible to consider a student for a new 
scholarship award once the degree programme has commenced.  
4.3 If a Scholarship has been awarded, the fee discount will be applied to the 
student’s tuition fee liability. Aston Scholarships will normally be available only 
to students who have been in attendance, as defined by the University 
throughout term one and term two and are still in attendance at the start of 
term three. Students who withdraw from Aston University part way through an 
academic year will not be eligible to receive a scholarship in respect of that year. 
Any tuition fee discount applied to the student for that academic year as the 
result of an Aston Scholarship will be withdrawn and the student will be liable 
for the full cost for that period.  
4.4 Students who are repeating any modules within the programme are not eligible 
for scholarships regardless of whether they are repeating with attendance, 
without attendance, or with partial attendance.   4.5 Where a student suspends their studies and takes a Leave of Absence for a 
complete academic year (i.e. October to October) no tuition fee is charged and, 
therefore, the student will not be eligible to receive a scholarship.  
4.6 Students who suspend their studies part way through an academic year and take 
a Leave of Absence will be eligible to receive a scholarship for the academic 
terms they have completed in full. The amount of the scholarship will be 
calculated on a pro rata basis and in line with Aston University’s Tuition Fees 
Charging Policy.  
4.7 Scholarships are valid for study on a taught programme at Aston University, 
Birmingham Campus and are not transferable to another campus or University.  
4.7.1 Specific programmes are excluded from this scholarships schemes 
unless otherwise stated. The affected programmes are: 
1. MBCHB in Medicine 
2. PGDIP/ MSC in OSPAP 
3. MSC in Physician Associate Practice 
4.8 The scholarships are valid for programmes of study commencing in the academic 
year 2025/26 only and cannot be carried forward to another academic year.  
4.9 Scholarships are valid for the specified programme of study at Aston University 
and may not normally be transferred to a different programme.  
4.10  Any evidence submitted after the final decision on the student’s eligibility 
has been made will not be considered, unless the student can demonstrate 
there was a good reason why the information could not be made available at the 
time of submitting the scholarship application.  
4.11 The decision of the awarding panel is final. Applicants may appeal against 
the decision only if they can show that there has been a procedural error. 
Appeals should be addressed to the Director of Student and Academic Services.
